title: Riftveil Report
description: Structured form of a Riftveil Protocol report (v1.0.0). Riftveil challenges an AI-generated output so a human can decide; it never validates, never rewrites, never concludes. A report is a set of findings, assumptions and open questions, not a verdict. Optional parts: an owner per question, the "before_this_runs" block for agent plans (with its reach), the closing line, the "independence" flag, "highest_value_question" (the Record box), the "attestation" object (the follow-up block, completed by the human, output on request only), the "metrics" object a team can aggregate, and "context.triage_criteria" (the Criteria line of section 1). A financial commitment given only as an amount, without the size of the organisation ("not stated (amount without scale)" in the Criteria line), is recorded as "not_stated". An input stopped by the input gate produces no report, and therefore no JSON form.

protocol_version.description: Version of the Riftveil Protocol used to produce the report, e.g. "1.0.0".

language.description: Optional BCP 47 tag of the language the report is written in ("en", "fr"). Riftveil answers in the user's language.

independence.description: Optional. The independence line of the Record box: whether the second reader ran on a different model family from the author, in a different session with no access to the authoring conversation, or in the same session as the author (findings are then a first pass, not a second reader). "not_stated": the user did not say which model or session produced the project; the line reads "not stated by the user, to be confirmed by the signer".

most_useful_question.description: Optional. The Record box line "Most useful question:": the one question from section 5 whose answer would most change the decision, quoted.

what_holds_up.description: Section 2. Two to four sentences on elements that are internally consistent. Diagnostic scope, never praise (Rule 1 applies): it tells the reader where NOT to spend verification effort.

findings.description: Section 3. What deserves scrutiny, ordered by descending impact regardless of level. When Level 2 is applied, the report opens this section with the Level 2 note (see level_2_note).

level_2_note.description: Optional. Present when Level 2 was applied: the one-line caveat that opens section 3 (an AI model does not reason in the human sense; the reasoning checks test logical consistency, not the process that produced the project).

assumptions.description: Section 4. Assumptions the output relies on.

questions.description: Section 5. Open questions before the human decides. Each must be specific to this output, answerable by the user from their context, and decision-relevant. 5-8 at MODERATE and above, 3 at LOW, 1-2 for inputs under 100 words. This is the last section: the report ends on a question (or on the permitted closing line).

closing_line.description: Optional. The only sentence permitted after the questions, in the report's language.
enum: No verdict. The decision is yours.
Aucun verdict. La décision vous appartient.

self_awareness_note.description: Rule 4. A statement that this challenge was produced by an AI sharing structural limitations with the system that produced the output, and that the human's contextual knowledge is the final arbiter.

focused_sections.description: Optional. For very long inputs (>2000 words), the sections the challenge focused on and why.

inferred_domain.description: Domain the output belongs to, e.g. "commercial strategy", "pharma regulatory", "software architecture".

inferred_role.description: Role or audience the output seems written for, e.g. "leadership team", "market access manager".

decision_type.description: Decision the output is informing, e.g. "market entry", "vendor selection", "regulatory submission".

stakes_level.description: Triage outcome. LOW = L1 only; MODERATE = L0-2; HIGH = L0-3; CRITICAL = L0-4.

triage_rationale.description: Why this stakes level: reversibility, impact scope, financial commitment. State it if stakes could not be inferred and MODERATE was applied by default.

context_supplied_by_user.description: Optional. True when the user stated role, stakes or decision explicitly and Riftveil used that instead of inferring.

triage_criteria.description: Optional. The Criteria line of section 1, which makes the escalation rule checkable: "Criteria: reversibility [LEVEL] · impact scope [LEVEL] · financial commitment [LEVEL] → [rule applied] → [TRIAGE]". The triage is the highest criterion, or CRITICAL when two or more are at HIGH or above; stakes_level carries the result.

stated_by_user.description: Optional. The criteria read from the user's own context, marked "(stated)" in the report.

rule_applied.description: Optional. The rule as written in the report, e.g. "highest single criterion" or "two criteria at HIGH or above".

criterion_level.description: Level read for one triage criterion, or "not_stated" when neither the project nor the user's context gives it; it also records a financial commitment given only as an amount, without the size of the organisation ("not stated (amount without scale)" in the report).

label.description: One-line, specific label for the finding.

technique_id.description: Technique that produced the finding, e.g. "2.1" (assumption surfacing). Format: <level>.<technique>.

observed.description: The "Observed:" line: a concrete observation drawn from the project.

effect_on_decision.description: The "Effect on the decision:" line: the specific consequence for the decision if this is not addressed.

to_check.description: The "To check:" line: an actionable step for the human, "verify X with Y", never "be careful".

impact.description: Estimated impact on the decision if the finding is left unaddressed. Findings are ordered by this, descending.

if_false.description: What changes if the assumption is false: a specific consequence.

who_can_verify.description: A person or function in the user's context who can verify it. Never "do more AI research".

stated_in_output.description: Optional. True if the output acknowledged this assumption; false if it was unstated.

question.description: A question before the decision. Either a plain string or an object carrying the optional owner hint.
The question, as a direct question with no preamble.

owner.description: Optional. The role in the user's context that can answer it ("finance controller", "head of operations"). Only when the role is inferable from the context; never invented.

before_this_runs.description: Mandatory in a report on an agent plan or a set of proposed actions (pre-action review); omitted otherwise. Sits between sections 4 and 5. Riftveil never approves execution: the stop condition is a condition for the human to check, not a permission. It carries an optional reach line.

irreversible_steps.description: Each step that cannot be undone once executed, or that acts outside the organisation, with what it touches.

missing_checkpoints.description: Points in the sequence where a human should look before the next step runs and the plan does not provide for it.

agent_assumptions.description: What the agent assumed about the permissions it holds, the data it read, and the current state of the systems and people it will act on.

stop_condition.description: One observable condition under which the human should halt execution. Stated as a condition to check, never as "safe to run".

reach.description: Optional. The widest audience any step of the plan touches once it runs. Organisation-wide or external: triage at least HIGH; irreversible and external: CRITICAL.

reach_set_by.description: Optional. The step that sets the reach.

attestation.description: Optional. The follow-up block: completed by the human, never by the model, output on request only. It certifies nothing; it is where the human notes what they did with the report. The model outputs the empty template only; a filed record carries the signer's own words. All fields optional strings.

checked_by_human.description: "I checked myself: [what, which source]" (written by the signer).

assigned.description: "Open questions assigned to: [role, question numbers]" (written by the signer).

record_id.description: Record ID in the team's decision file (written by the signer).

signed_at.description: Date of the follow-up note, ISO 8601 preferred (written by the human).

metrics.description: Optional. Record metrics as defined in the protocol's <record_metrics> block: every value is derivable from the report itself, for monthly aggregation by a team. None is a score of the output.

findings_total.description: Number of findings in section 3 (length of findings[]).

findings_by_impact.description: Findings split by impact, from findings[].impact.

findings_by_challenge_level.description: Findings split by challenge level 0-4, from findings[].level.

assumptions_with_verifier.description: Assumptions whose who_can_verify names a human role.

assumptions_without_verifier.description: Assumptions whose verifier line is missing, names the AI, or names no role. The protocol requires zero.

attestation_present.description: True when the filed record carries a follow-up block (`attestation` object) with at least one line filled in by the human; the empty template does not count.

same_session_as_author.description: True only when independence is "same_session": the findings are a first pass, not a second reader.
